methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $235M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Electra.aero is a Series B transportation company founded by John Langford, having raised $235M to date. The broader Transportation sector comprises 7 private comparable companies (including Rivian, The Boring Company, and Einride), with no public peers available for direct benchmarking.

The Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable valuation approach. Using total capital raised of $235M as a proxy for post-money valuation, a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement yields an implied valuation of $446M. This reflects the expected value accretion between Series B and the subsequent financing stage. The Peer-Median method could not be applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the Transportation cohort; applying an all-sector median would introduce material bias and was therefore excluded from the analysis.

The triangulated valuation range is $380M (low) to $513M (high), with a median of $446M. This narrow single-method result carries elevated uncertainty given reliance on stage-progression mechanics rather than cross-corroboration with peer multiples. Key risks to valuation include execution risk on aircraft development timelines, regulatory approval paths specific to electric aviation, and limited precedent for comparable stage transitions in this subsector. Additional data on peer financings and nearer-stage Transportation comparables would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
